reading.title: Walk After the Rain
reading.purpose: Follow Tessa and her grandfather as they notice lights and sounds on a wet evening walk.
paras: Right after the rain stopped, Tessa and her grandpa went out for a walk. Fresh air smelled like wet pine, and the whole street looked washed clean.

Puddles made the brick path glisten, shining because each stone was wet. Ahead, porch lamps began to flicker, blinking on and off in the soft breeze. On the shop door, bright brass bars seemed to gleam under the street lights.

Near the park bridge, they stopped to watch the creek. Pale leaves began to drift past, carried slow by the water. Down the path, string lights looked radiant, glowing bright in the dusk. Their glow made the creek shimmer with a soft, trembling light.

Then the night grew loud. A big truck rolled over the bridge and made the planks rumble with a deep, rolling sound. Someone dropped metal trays in the lane, and they hit with a sharp clatter. Steam rose from a grate and began to hiss like a pot. When Tessa called "Hello!" under the stone arch, her voice seemed to echo right back.
"Rain turns a plain street into a show," Grandpa smiled, and Tessa agreed.

choices: to make a loud noise like falling metal trays
to shine because a surface is wet
to move slowly down a flowing creek
to bounce back a voice under a stone arch
qs.why: Paragraph 2 says puddles made the brick path glisten, "shining because every stone was wet."

qs.q: Which sentence shows what caused a clatter in the lane?
choices: A big truck rolled over the bridge and made the planks rumble with a deep, rolling sound.
Someone dropped metal trays in the lane, and they hit with a sharp clatter.
Steam rose from a grate and began to hiss like a pot.
qs.why: This sentence tells that dropped metal trays hitting the ground caused the sharp clatter.

ev.text: Someone dropped metal trays in the lane, and they hit with a sharp clatter.

qs.q: Why did Grandpa say rain turns a plain street into a show?
choices: A real band was playing loud music on the wooden park bridge all night.
The wet street was full of bright lights and vivid sounds.
Tessa was afraid of the dark and wanted to hurry straight home to bed.
The shop gave out free snacks to every walker right after the storm.
qs.why: Throughout the walk, Tessa and Grandpa watched glistening paths, shimmering water, and heard rumbles, hisses, and echoes.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: How a big truck crosses a wooden park bridge during a heavy rainstorm
Why metal trays should never be carried through a wet lane after dark
A girl and her grandpa noticing lights and sounds after rain
How to hang bright string lights over a creek before sunset each fall
qs.why: The story follows Tessa and Grandpa enjoying all the lights and sounds on their after-rain walk.

clues.text: shining because each stone was wet
